Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
529 AM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Unsettled pattern prevails through Friday with several 
rounds of showers expected, with greatest concentration over the 
higher terrain.

2. Cooler and drier weather develops late Friday into Saturday, 
with patchy frost possible in the Champlain Valley on Saturday 
morning. 

3. Remnants of tropical system to bring rain to parts of our 
region.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper level low slowly builds into the region today 
and tomorrow, bringing several rounds of showers as shortwaves pivot 
around the longwave trough. Instability will reach its maximum today 
and some of the stronger showers will likely contain thunder. Pea 
sized hail will be possible, and maybe graupel in the higher 
terrain. The highest chances for showers will be farther north where 
the better dynamics and coldest air aloft will be. A lowering 
inversion heading into Friday should prevent any thunder chances, 
with instability only reaching up to around 10,000 feet and not 
significantly surpassing -10 Celsius. However, the airmass will 
continue to cool and temperatures at the summits are expected to 
fall below freezing on Friday, so a few flurries/snow showers will 
be possible in the mountains, especially farther north. Snow levels 
look to drop to around 3,500-4,000 feet. Flow remains unblocked 
heading through Friday as the inversion will stay well above summit 
level.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure builds in for the weekend, leading 
to a couple classic fall days. Highs will be in the 50s and 60s with 
mostly sunny skies. Radiational cooling conditions will become 
somewhat favorable for Friday night, but some lingering boundary 
flow may prevent the most efficient temperature decreases. The 
boundary layer looks to decouple at least in the later part of the 
night though. Frost formation is expected across most of the region, 
but it looks more uncertain in the Champlain Valley, the only area 
left in the growing season. Temperatures there will be marginal and 
winds there will likely hold on the longest.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The remnants of Isaias will bring some rain to southern 
portions of our forecast area Sunday night into Monday. Not 
expecting any strong winds with this system. Northern extent of 
precipitation is uncertain. For now have highest chances for 
precipitation from Saranac Lake NY to Montpelier VT and areas south 
of there.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 06Z Friday...A line of showers with some embedded
thunder moving across the area, briefly bringing some areas down
to MVFR conditions. Strength and intensity of showers has been
decreasing. S/SW winds remain breezy, especially at BTV where 
gusts around 20 kt continue ahead of the front. Winds will 
decrease a bit, the gusts should mostly be below 20 kt as the
night wears on. 

Outlook...

Friday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA.
Columbus Day: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory continues with sustained southerly winds
between 20-30 KT. Winds will turn southwesterly and then
westerly this morning, and will then drop into the 10-20 KT 
range. Wave heights will drop from the 1-3 foot range to below 2
feet after this wind shift occurs. 

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
